content.text:
The alert wasn't a bug in Mark Shipped at all — it was your farmer login session silently dying underneath a dashboard that kept looking logged in.

## Why it happened

Farmer auth has two halves that could drift apart:

- The **`yff_farmer` cookie** (HTTP-only, 30-day expiry) is what every farmer API route actually checks.
- **`localStorage.yff_farmer_id`** is what every farmer *page* checked to decide "are you logged in?"

localStorage never expires. The cookie does — after 30 days, or whenever the browser clears cookies (Chrome on Android does this on its own). Once that happened, the dashboard and orders list rendered perfectly, because they only ever looked at localStorage. But the moment the farmer tapped **Mark Shipped**, `POST /api/farmer/orders/[id]/ship` found no cookie and answered `401 {"error":"Please log in."}` — and the page dumped that straight into an `alert()`. No redirect, no way out. Same trap on Confirm Pickup, Confirm Delivery, Decline, Acknowledge, Save Listing, and Change Password.

I confirmed it against a running server with a real forged-but-valid token for farmer "veeru": a 31-day-old token is rejected by `/api/auth/me` while the page would still have rendered from localStorage.

## What I changed

**The cookie is now the only credential.** A new `src/lib/farmer-auth-client.ts` gives every farmer page two entry points:

- `requireFarmerSession()` runs on page load and verifies against `/api/auth/me`. No session means you land on the login page, not a dashboard where nothing works. It also handles the reverse case — valid cookie, evicted localStorage — by re-seeding the cache instead of logging you out.
- `farmerFetch()` wraps every farmer write. A 401 now clears the stale id and redirects to login instead of raising an alert.

**Sessions no longer expire under an active farmer.** `/api/auth/me` re-issues the cookie with a fresh 30-day window once it's more than a day old. Verified: a 1-hour-old token gets no new cookie, a 10-day-old one gets re-issued, a 31-day-old one is rejected.

**The login page explains itself.** Bouncing there shows "Your session ended. Please log in again to continue." and returns the farmer to the page they were kicked off (validated to in-app `/farmer/` paths only, so it can't be used as an open redirect).

Two things I found along the way and fixed: farmer **logout never cleared the server cookie** — it only wiped localStorage, leaving a live session on the device — so I added `POST /api/auth/logout`. And since the Trello card was blocked on this, I also did what it actually asked: the Shipped banner now reads **"Shipped on Fri, 10 Jul, 2026, 04:03 pm"** under "Shipped — on the way", using the same date format as the rest of the card, on both the home-delivery and courier variants.

Build passes and lint is unchanged at 19 pre-existing findings. Nothing is committed or pushed yet — say the word and I'll commit.

One thing worth deciding: the **moderator and rider modules have their own session cookies**, and I didn't audit whether they gate their pages the same localStorage-only way. Given your farmer↔moderator parity rule, that's probably worth a look before real user testing.

Done. The rating badge now navigates, and the profile page understands where to land.

The badge on the farmer dashboard was rendered as a plain `<div>` — nothing was clickable, which is exactly what the tester hit. Two changes make it work:

**`TabSection` now accepts a `?tab=` deep link.** It reads a stable, language-independent slug (`story`, `produce`, `quality`, `reviews`, `farm`) and opens on that tab, falling back to Harvests for a missing or unrecognized value. I used a language-independent slug deliberately: the tab labels are translated, so keying the URL off the visible label would break the link in Telugu. On arrival it scrolls down to the tab strip — offset by the sticky header — so a deep link lands on the reviews themselves rather than the hero image above them. That scroll runs only on first paint, otherwise it would yank the page every time the farmer switched tabs by hand.

**The rating badge is now a `Link` to `/farmer/[slug]?tab=reviews`,** with the review count underlined so it reads as tappable, plus an aria-label.

I verified this against a running server with a real farmer profile:

| URL | Active tab |
|---|---|
| `/farmer/veeru-3ox` | Harvests |
| `/farmer/veeru-3ox?tab=reviews` | Reviews |
| `/farmer/veeru-3ox?tab=story` | About Farm |
| `/farmer/veeru-3ox?tab=bogus` | Harvests |

The `?tab=reviews` page renders the review-writing UI and the star ratings; the default page doesn't. Build passes, types clean, and `TabSection` actually drops a lint finding (it had an unused `useEffect` import that I now use).

Worth flagging one thing about my own process: partway through I saw the profile page return 404 and briefly thought I'd broken it. I hadn't — my earlier `npm run build` had overwritten the `.next` directory out from under the running dev server. Re-testing on a clean server gave 200. I'm noting it because the check that caught it was comparing against stashed `main`, which is the only reason I didn't report a phantom regression.
